title: SpinePrep: a containerised BIDS-App for reproducible spinal-cord fMRI preprocessing

creators.name: Sharifi, Kiomars
creators.affiliation: ETH Zurich; University of Zurich; Balgrist University Hospital

description:
SpinePrep is an open, containerised BIDS-App for reproducible preprocessing of human spinal-cord fMRI. A BIDS dataset goes in; GLM-ready derivatives and per-step quality control come out.

The pipeline runs ten steps end to end — input verification, anatomical cord reference, functional reference and cord-focused crop, motion correction, distortion correction, functional-to-anatomical registration, PAM50 template normalization, confounds and physiological regressors, GLM-ready derivatives with per-vertebral-level tSNR, and QC aggregation with a reproducibility receipt. Each step measures itself in isolation and emits its own diagnostic reportlet, so a failure is attributable to the step that caused it.

The scientific methods belong to the tools SpinePrep integrates — the Spinal Cord Toolbox, FSL, ANTs, and the PAM50 template. SpinePrep's contribution is the integration, automation, reproducibility, and standardised quality control around them, not new algorithms.

Please cite SpinePrep alongside the underlying tools (SCT, FSL, ANTs, PAM50). The auto-generated methods boilerplate in each run's report lists the ones that run actually used.
